title: Cancellation and regrouping of finite coproduct cocones
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations, mapping spaces and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in fixed sufficiently large universes. Let $\mathcal E$ be a quasicategory, let $S$ be a finite set, and for each $s\in S$ let $R_s$ be a finite set and $x_{sr}$ vertices of $\mathcal E$. Suppose specified legs $u_{sr}:x_{sr}\to y_s$ form a colimiting cocone on the discrete diagram $(x_{sr})_{r\in R_s}$, for every $s$. Given legs $v_s:y_s\to z$, choose composites $w_{sr}:x_{sr}\to z$ and $2$-simplices witnessing $w_{sr}\simeq v_su_{sr}$. Then the $v_s$ form a coproduct cocone if and only if the $w_{sr}$ form a coproduct cocone on the discrete family indexed by $\coprod_{s\in S}R_s$. More precisely, for every test vertex $t$, the triangle of whole mapping spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(z,t)\longrightarrow\prod_s\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(y_s,t)\longrightarrow\prod_s\prod_{r\in R_s}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x_{sr},t)$$
is homotopy commutative, where the first map restricts along the $v_s$, the second restricts along the $u_{sr}$, and the composite is restriction along the $w_{sr}$. The second map is an equivalence, naturally in $t$, including all higher simplices. Both the empty $S$ and empty blocks $R_s$ are allowed. No colimits other than the specified block coproducts are assumed.

source.place: Kerodon Subsection 7.6.1, the colimit dual of Proposition 7.6.1.23 and its preservation remark; finite discrete blocks with specified composition triangles. Agent-formulated mapping-space cancellation refinement. No Stacks tag states this coherent assertion.

proof.text:
For a finite discrete set $I$ and diagram $a:I\to\mathcal E$, the internal functor simplicial set is the degreewise product $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)=\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal E$: a map $I\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$ is one $n$-simplex per $i$. The right-pinched definition then gives a simplicial isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)}(a,\Delta_I t)=\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(a_i,t).$$
Indeed in degree $n$ both sides specify the same family of maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal E$ with constant initial face at $a_i$ and last vertex $t$; all operators restrict each coordinate. Under this isomorphism the map $g\mapsto\Delta_I(g)\circ\lambda$ of the cocone criterion, for specified legs $\lambda_i:a_i\to b$, is coordinatewise precomposition $f\mapsto(f\lambda_i)_i$ up to homotopy: the spaces $V$, the edge restrictions $\theta,\ell$ and the right-pinch inclusions $j$ (all defined by restriction or precomposition of simplices) characterizing the canonical composition class in the mapping-composition theorem are, for the product quasicategory $\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal E$, the products of those for $\mathcal E$, so that characterization makes the composition class of $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)$ the product of those of $\mathcal E$. The functor and mapping spaces are quasicategories and Kan complexes, respectively, by the cone-calculus theorem. Thus its dual cocone criterion says that specified legs $a_i\to b$ are colimiting exactly when restriction $\operatorname{Map}(b,t)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Map}(a_i,t)$ is an equivalence for every $t$. This applies to $I=\varnothing$ as well: both the functor category and the empty product of mapping spaces are the point.

source.place: Definitions 7.6.1.1 and 7.6.1.3 and Remark 7.6.1.5, dual cocone version; agent expansion for the specified right-pinched convention.

proof.text:
Fix a test vertex $t$. Apply Step 1 to each specified block cocone $u_s$. Its colimiting hypothesis makes the actual restriction map
$$\beta_{s,t}:\operatorname{Map}(y_s,t)\longrightarrow\prod_{r\in R_s}\operatorname{Map}(x_{sr},t)$$
a weak equivalence of Kan complexes. No block coproduct is constructed or chosen here: its vertex and all legs are precisely the given $y_s,u_{sr}$. For $R_s=\varnothing$ this says $\operatorname{Map}(y_s,t)\to *$ is a weak equivalence, exactly the initial-object condition.

source.place: Remark 7.6.1.5 and Example 7.6.1.8, dual mapping-space criterion applied to the assumed block cocones.

proof.text: The map $\beta_t=\prod_s\beta_{s,t}$ is a weak equivalence. Here is a short reduction to the cited homotopy-pullback invariance statement, rather than an additional product-preservation assertion. Over the one-point Kan complex the displayed path-space pullback $P(U\to *,V\to *)$ is exactly $U\times V$, since $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,*)=*$ degreewise. Apply that statement to two weak equivalences and the identity of $*$: all cospan squares commute strictly, so their product map is a weak equivalence. Induction on the number of elements of $S$, starting with $*\xrightarrow{1}*$, gives the claim. The products remain Kan because any horn is filled one coordinate at a time. Finally the map $(a_{sr})\mapsto((a_{sr})_{r\in R_s})_{s\in S}$ identifies the single product indexed by $\coprod_s R_s$ with the iterated product in every simplicial degree, with inverse evaluation at $(s,r)$.

source.place: Proposition 7.6.1.23, dual: elementary finite-product reduction of the block mapping-space equivalences.

proof.text:
Write $\alpha_t(f)=(fv_s)_s$ and $\gamma_t(f)=(fw_{sr})_{s,r}$ for restriction along the specified outer and flattened legs. The mapping-composition theorem makes these maps on the whole Kan mapping spaces, interpreted up to simplicial homotopy. For each $(s,r)$ it gives the homotopy $ (fv_s)u_{sr}\simeq f(v_su_{sr})$ from associativity. The specified $2$-simplex gives $[w_{sr}]=[v_s][u_{sr}]$, and restriction depends only on this component class; consequently $f(v_su_{sr})\simeq fw_{sr}$ as maps with variable $f\in\operatorname{Map}(z,t)$. Take these finitely many homotopies coordinatewise. Their composite in the homotopy category of Kan complexes yields
$$\beta_t\alpha_t\simeq\gamma_t.$$
Thus the triangle compares actual restriction maps on entire mapping spaces, not just maps on components. No compatibility between different $(s,r)$ is demanded, because the indexing diagram is discrete.

source.place: Proposition 7.6.1.23, dual, with composition comparison expanded using Kerodon Subsection 4.6.8 (01PF).

proof.text: These constructions retain the variable $t$ coherently. Choose a universe containing all mapping spaces and a further one containing $\mathcal E$. The Hom-bifunctor theorem gives $H_{\mathcal E}:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal E\to\mathcal S$ with its canonical unit and composition homotopies. Each $u_{sr}$ therefore gives a coherent natural transformation $H(y_s,-)\to H(x_{sr},-)$; its value at $t$ is restriction by $u_{sr}$. Taking the finite coordinate product gives precisely $\beta$ with values $\beta_t$. In every simplicial parameter, the product is a tuple of the same component data, with faces and degeneracies componentwise. The same construction gives $\alpha$ and $\gamma$, and applying $H$ to the given composition triangles supplies their comparison. This proves the asserted naturality in $t$ with higher simplices retained, without choosing inverses separately at each $t$. Step 3 proves that every component of this natural comparison $\beta$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 7.6.1.23 and its preservation/naturality interpretation; coherent naturality is supplied by the existing Hom bifunctor, not inferred from vertex values.

proof.text: For every $t$, Step 3 makes $\beta_t$ a weak equivalence and Step 4 identifies $\gamma_t$ with $\beta_t\alpha_t$ up to homotopy. Weak equivalences obey two-out-of-three in the Kan-Quillen model structure. Homotopic maps have the same weak-equivalence property: their realized maps are homotopic, so induce the same component map and conjugate maps on based homotopy groups along the basepoint track. Hence $\alpha_t$ is a weak equivalence if and only if $\gamma_t$ is. Apply the dual cocone criterion of Step 1, first to the family $(y_s)_s$ and then to $(x_{sr})_{(s,r)}$, to conclude the required if and only if. If $S=\varnothing$, $\beta_t$ is the identity of $*$ and both conditions say that $z$ is initial. Empty blocks have already been included in Step 2; in particular if every block is empty both criteria still compare with the empty flattened family. Only the supplied block colimits were used.

lean.statement: theorem finite_coproduct_regrouping (E : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory E] (S : Type u) [Finite S] (R : S → Type u) [∀ s, Finite (R s)] (x : ∀ s, R s → E _⦋0⦌) (y : S → E _⦋0⦌) (z : E _⦋0⦌) (u : ∀ s r, (mappingSpace E (x s r) (y s)) _⦋0⦌) (hu : ∀ s, IsColimiting (regroupingDiagram (x s)) (regroupingCocone (u s))) (v : ∀ s, (mappingSpace E (y s) z) _⦋0⦌) (w : ∀ p : Sigma R, (mappingSpace E (x p.1 p.2) z) _⦋0⦌) (triangles : ∀ s, R s → E _⦋2⦌) (htriangles : ∀ s r, E.δ 2 (triangles s r) = (u s r).1 ∧ E.δ 0 (triangles s r) = (v s).1 ∧ E.δ 1 (triangles s r) = (w ⟨s, r⟩).1) : (IsColimiting (regroupingDiagram y) (regroupingCocone v) ↔ IsColimiting (regroupingDiagram (fun p : Sigma R ↦ x p.1 p.2)) (regroupingCocone w)) ∧ (∀ t : E _⦋0⦌, Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (regroupingRestriction v t ≫ regroupingBlockRestriction u t) (regroupingRestriction w t ≫ regroupingProductMap x t)) ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (regroupingBlockRestriction u t)) ∧ ∀ s, RegroupingBlockNaturality (u s)
